top3.headline: Anthropic drops the 5-hour limit on its $200 Claude Ultra plan
top3.whyItMatters: Heavy Claude Code users can now run long sessions without hitting a midday wall.

top3.headline: OpenRouter now routes by real cost, not sticker price
top3.whyItMatters: Cheapest listed price is not cheapest in production; ask how your vendors route.

top3.headline: Supabase says about 70% of its new activity comes from agents
top3.whyItMatters: Agents now drive most new usage on a major developer platform; build for them.

items.title: a16z: AI job-loss news is down about 65% from last year
items.takeaway: Layoff announcements citing AI fell about 90%, while engineering job postings rose about 30%, per Indeed data.
items.soWhat: The AI layoff story is cooling in the data, so plan hiring on demand, not headlines.

image.alt: Image from a16z Charts of the Week

items.title: Anthropic drops the 5-hour limit on its $200 Claude Ultra plan
items.takeaway: Max 20x becomes Ultra at $200 a month; verified accounts lose the 5-hour cap, weekly limits stay.
items.soWhat: Heavy Claude Code users can now run long sessions without hitting a midday wall.

items.title: Google ran a prompt on a TPU in orbit
items.takeaway: Project Suncatcher's prototype satellite booted its TPU and sent back a full response on command.
items.soWhat: Space-based compute moved from concept to a working test, an early sign for future capacity.

items.title: OpenAI launches Private Intelligence for tighter enterprise data control
items.takeaway: Built with some of its largest customers; OpenAI gave no technical or pricing detail yet.
items.soWhat: Data control is now a selling point for frontier models; ask vendors for specifics.

items.title: Perplexity's agent can now drive your own signed-in Chrome
items.takeaway: A new extension lets Perplexity Computer on Mac and Windows work inside sites you are already logged into.
items.soWhat: Agents acting in staff browser sessions inherit their access, so set policy before rollout.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV urges UN steps toward banning autonomous weapons
items.takeaway: He said AI should be disarmed and decisions on life and force must stay under human oversight.
items.soWhat: Pressure for human oversight rules is widening beyond tech regulators ahead of Geneva talks.

items.title: Supabase says about 70% of its new activity comes from agents
items.takeaway: CEO Paul Copplestone told YC's Lightcone it has 13M users and spins up over a million databases weekly.
items.soWhat: Developer platforms are now being chosen by agents, so design products for them too.

items.title: Meng To designs a three.js landing page with Opus 5.5
items.takeaway: He shared his workflow for the mischief-1 video model page, built from three.js concepts.
items.soWhat: Designers can now prototype rich 3D web concepts with a model before committing build time.

items.title: Anthropic's S-1 runs 94 pages of risk factors
items.takeaway: The Verge read the 335-page filing, whose founders' letter asks buyers not to think purely transactionally.
items.soWhat: Investors are being asked to buy a mission as much as a business.

items.title: Lyn Alden: local AI needs only a nontrivial share of users
items.takeaway: Some businesses and people need local setups for privacy or for work central providers might block.
items.soWhat: Plan for both cloud and on-premise AI; each wins in different contexts.

items.title: Research agents proposed 415 experiments; only 73 were truly novel
items.takeaway: rTaste found six frontier models rarely pick experiments beyond the seed paper, and teams cost more.
items.soWhat: Agents can generate research ideas cheaply, but judging which matter still needs people.

image.alt: arXiv 2610.40488: Research agents proposed 415 experiments; only 73 were truly novel

items.title: Opus 5 failed 16 of 16 tasks when facts changed mid-task
items.takeaway: EnvOS tests agents in changing environments; a reminder to re-check lifted success only to 2 of 16.
items.soWhat: Agents trust what they read first, so build in fresh lookups before they act.

image.alt: arXiv 2610.40246: Opus 5 failed 16 of 16 tasks when facts changed mid-task

items.title: OpenRouter now routes by real cost, not sticker price
items.takeaway: Ranking providers by effective price, wait and retry cost gave 16.9% faster first tokens for 6% more spend.
items.soWhat: The cheapest listed model provider is often not the cheapest one to run in production.

voices.quote: We're removing the 5-hour limit for verified Ultra accounts.
This is smart. Wild that this wasn’t the default. Unpredictable inference quality was usually why I recommended skipping the middleman.
your codebase is becoming organic architecture. agent contributions grow around the constraints and guardrails you’ve designed. good software engineering matters even more now!
just ask your agent to do any local browsing tasks on your Chrome browser

hotOnX.text: Claude Code reportedly got a server-side rule against recreating specific existing games, with no setting to turn it off.
hotOnX.note: An unconfirmed claim that revived debate over vendors changing agent rules remotely.

hotOnX.text: Project Suncatcher's satellite booted its TPU in orbit, ran a prompt from Earth and sent back a haiku.
hotOnX.note: A first working test of AI compute in space.

hotOnX.text: Much software must be rebuilt so agents can work safely at a continuous pace: make the easy thing the right thing.
hotOnX.note: Engineers see codebase design as the main lever for safe agent contributions.

hotOnX.text: Max 20x is now Ultra at $200 a month, and verified Ultra accounts lose the 5-hour usage limit.
hotOnX.note: Removes a cap that cut long agent sessions short.

hotOnX.text: OpenAI Private Intelligence gives businesses stronger controls over their data while using its most capable models.
hotOnX.note: Enterprises want frontier models without giving up data control.
